verses.text: And Samuel's word came to all Israel. Now the Israelites went out to fight against the Philistines. The Israelites camped at Ebenezer, and the Philistines at Aphek.
The Philistines lined up for battle to face Israel. As the battle spread, Israel was defeated by the Philistines, who killed about four thousand of them on the battlefield.

When the soldiers came back to camp, the elders of Israel asked, "Why did the LORD let the Philistines defeat us today? Let us bring the covenant box of the LORD here from Shiloh, so that it may go with us and save us from our enemies."

So the people sent men to Shiloh, and they brought back the covenant box of the LORD of Heaven's Armies, who sits on his throne between the cherubim. Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, were there with the covenant box of God.
When the covenant box of the LORD came into the camp, all Israel gave such a loud shout that the ground shook.
Hearing the noise, the Philistines asked, "What is all this shouting in the Hebrew camp?" When they learned that the box of the LORD had come into the camp,
the Philistines were afraid. "A god has come into their camp," they said. "Oh no! Nothing like this has happened before.
We are in trouble! Who will save us from the power of these mighty gods? They are the gods who struck the Egyptians with all kinds of plagues in the desert.
Be strong, Philistines! Be men, or you will become slaves of the Hebrews, as they have been your slaves. Be men, and fight!"
So the Philistines fought, and the Israelites were defeated, and every man ran back to his tent. It was a terrible defeat. Israel lost thirty thousand foot soldiers.
The box of God was captured, and Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, died.
That same day a man from the tribe of Benjamin ran from the battle line and went to Shiloh. His clothes were torn, and there was dust on his head.

When he arrived, Eli was sitting on his chair by the side of the road, watching, because his heart was worried about the box of God. When the man came into the town and told what had happened, the whole town cried out.
Eli heard the crying and asked, "What is all this noise?" The man hurried over to Eli
who was ninety-eight years old and whose eyes had stopped working so that he could not see.
He told Eli, "I have just come from the battle line. I ran from it this very day." Eli asked, "What happened, my son?"

The man who brought the news replied, "Israel ran away from the Philistines, and the army has suffered heavy losses. Your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, are dead, and the box of God has been captured."
When he mentioned the box of God, Eli fell backward off his chair by the side of the gate. His neck was broken, and he died, because he was old and heavy. He had led Israel for forty years.

His daughter-in-law, the wife of Phinehas, was pregnant and near the time of birth. When she heard the news that the box of God had been captured and that her father-in-law and her husband were dead, she went into labour and gave birth, overcome by her pains.
As she was dying, the women helping her said, "Do not be afraid. You have given birth to a son." But she did not answer or pay any attention.
She named the boy Ichabod, which means No Glory, saying, "The glory has left Israel." She said this because the box of God had been captured and because her father-in-law and her husband had died.
She said, "The glory has left Israel, because the box of God has been captured."
